Jianhua Zhao PhD: The Zhao lab studies how proteins work, and how that changes in disease, by looking at their physical shape and structure. Dr. Zhao specializes in cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a technique that flash-freezes protein samples and images them to reveal their three-dimensional structure at high resolution. Understanding a protein's precise shape helps explain how it normally functions and what goes wrong when disease occurs, which can point toward new therapeutic targets. Dr. Zhao's own training spans this kind of structural work: his PhD research examined rotary ATPases (molecular motors that help cells manage energy), and his postdoctoral work at UCSF focused on Transient Receptor Potential ion channels, proteins involved in sensing signals like temperature and pressure.
